title: Defensively copy SyncPushException.committed so the partial-commit invariant can't be violated by a future caller
rule: Evans lens — invariant enforced in one place, not by caller convention
why: SyncPushException.committed exists specifically so OutboxProcessor can tell which outbox rows genuinely landed before a batch failed, so committed rows are 'never re-pushed or dead-lettered' (per this file's own docstring, H3). That invariant currently holds only because the single production call site remembers to wrap the list in List.unmodifiable(pushed) before throwing — the exception class itself accepts any List<String>, including a live mutable reference, with no internal defensive copy. A future call site (or a test double standing in for one) that passes a growable list it keeps appending to after constructing the exception would silently corrupt the partial-commit accounting this type exists to protect, with no compiler or runtime signal that anything went wrong.
recommendation: Copy defensively inside the constructor (e.g. an initializer that wraps committed in List.unmodifiable(committed)) so the guarantee doesn't depend on every future caller remembering to do it themselves.
acceptance_criteria: a new unit test constructs SyncPushException with a growable list, mutates the original list after construction, and asserts .committed is unaffected
